- When sentiment is consistently high (>0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., <0.4) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is flat or low (0.3–0.6) and price is consolidating, model tends to lag; forecast should align with recent 5–7 day moving average.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a high sentiment period, model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
